messages:
sara.devex: Hey team — I'm writing CI onboarding scripts and need a recommended pattern for CLI auth across Linux/Mac/Windows. We need: ephemeral tokens rotated by pipeline, local dev using OS keyring, and a fallback file-based profile for headless VMs. What's the cleanest approach that works cross-platform?

Tom: +1 good question. Our usual pattern: prefer environment-variable override in CI, fallback to XDG/OS-specific credential file for non-CI. Keep keyring for interactive dev. So priority: 1) REDWOOD_TOKEN (or REDWOOD_PROFILE + token env), 2) XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood/credentials, 3) OS keyring.

Tom: Example for CI job (bash):
```bash
export REDWOOD_PROFILE=ci-worker
export REDWOOD_TOKEN=\"$SECRET_REDSHIFT_REDFLOW_TOKEN\" # from vault/secret manager
# if you want file fallback
mkdir -p "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood"
cat > "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood/credentials" <<EOF
[ci-worker]
token=$REDWOOD_TOKEN
EOF
```

alex.sdk: If you use ephemeral tokens, make sure the CLI supports a short-lived token refresh command in your pipeline step. We recommend doing an auth step at container start that exchanges the longer-lived pipeline secret for a temp token and writes it to REDWOOD_TOKEN env var. For example in GitHub Actions:
```yaml
- name: Get temp token
  run: |
    TEMP_TOKEN=$(vault read -field=token secret/redwood/ci)
    echo "REDWOOD_TOKEN=$TEMP_TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_ENV
- name: Run tests
  run: ./run-tests.sh
```
```
# or explicit CLI refresh (if using oauth):
redwood auth refresh --client-id $CI_CLIENT_ID --client-secret $CI_CLIENT_SECRET --out-env >> $GITHUB_ENV
```

sara.devex: Nice, couple clarifying q's — 1) Any gotchas on Windows runners (actions/windows-latest)? 2) Should we commit a sample credentials file in repo for devs?

Tom: Windows: prefer %APPDATA%/Redwood/credentials for file fallback, but if you always set REDWOOD_TOKEN in CI there isn't a problem. WSL: XDG paths work inside WSL. Avoid relying on OS keyring on CI.

Tom: For sample creds, commit a template like credentials.example with obviously fake values and a README explaining to never commit real tokens; use .gitignore for actual creds.

alex.sdk: Also watch streaming + retry behavior if tokens rotate mid-request — our runtime will return 401 on token expiry. Pattern: catch 401, call refresh (if available), and retry idempotent requests. For streaming sessions, prefer pre-warming a token and short-lived TTL rather than refresh mid-stream.

ci-bot: FYI docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/cli/auth (internal) :book:

sara.devex: Awesome — I'll draft a small repo scaffold: credentials.example, scripts/get-temp-token.sh, and a README. Will post PR. Thanks :thumbsup:

Tom: Thanks — ping me on the PR for Windows runner testing.

alex.sdk: happy to review the token-refresh bits.
